name: Chloris

project_scope.selection_mode: Five currently installed canonical manifest Chloris entries: species card FINISH/ENRICH
project_scope.range_status: Previously documented county native-range evidence remains UNCHANGED for all five installed Chloris entries; do not count previously range-unresolved taxa as confirmed target-zone natives.
project_scope.scientific_review_scope: Photo-led recognition and explicit hybrid uncertainty, no county native range audit
project_scope.note: Previous genus scope incorrectly counted only three installed canonical entries. Manifest also contains C. andropogonoides and C. × subdolichostachya. Species-level taxon photo determinations still remain provisional where originally flagged.

look_here_first: Trace the WHOLE FLOWERING AXIS, not merely one spikelet-bearing branch. Distinguish LONG SLIM radiating arms (C. andropogonoides), SHORT CROWDED racemes (C. cucullata), LONG arms on SEPARATED tiers (C. verticillata), a FEATHERY terminal fan (C. virgata), and a SOURCE-REPORTED intermediate hybrid candidate (C. × subdolichostachya). Then use 10–20× to see the fertile versus UPPER STERILE lemma, their awns, hood and hairs. None of the source images independently proves a confirmed hybrid or microscopic species ID.
shared_genus_traits: Warm-season grasses with radiating fingerlike racemes carrying spikelets along one side; the windmill silhouette alone is not species-diagnostic.
Each spikelet has glumes and a fertile floret with one or more reduced sterile florets above it. The fertile and sterile lemmas may bear different awns.
For species-level ID, examine a mature head plus a detached spikelet under 10–20× magnification and use a millimeter scale.

cautions: Never identify by purple or straw-colored heads alone; age changes color.
Raceme length and awn lengths overlap, especially between C. verticillata and C. virgata; use whorl arrangement, basal crown, and fertile lemma hairs together.
C. ×subdolichostachya is reported as a naturally occurring C. cucullata × C. verticillata hybrid. Intermediate heads should remain unresolved pending diagnostic review.
C. andropogonoides is in the Master Plant Pool but is not among these three canonical cards; avoid implying this key covers every local Chloris.
Do not use Texas state nativity to convert project county-level RANGE_UNRESOLVED into PASS.

lookalikes.difference: Source-pool Chloris with slender spike arrangement; needs targeted diagnostic review before adding a fourth key branch.
Natural C. cucullata × C. verticillata hybrid; may combine intermediate raceme and spikelet characters. Do not force either parent.
Also digitate grass heads, but Cynodon spikelets and branch layout differ; inspect spikelet under hand lens.
Radiating thick comb-like spikes, distinct spikelet shape; inspect branch tips and spikelet arrangement.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.look_for: Same-scale heads with arrows showing crowded whorls, spaced whorls, or terminal fan.
10–20× mature spikelet with arrow on upper sterile lemma and 1 mm scale.
Separate arrows for each lemma and its awn; measure in mm.
Matched side-lit macros with arrow to hairs near fertile lemma apex.
Plant base and lower nodes showing annual crown versus perennial rooting habit.
Future verified intermediate hybrid spikelet and whole head; no generic substitution.

diagnostic_photo_checklist: Get separate measured FERTILE lemma awn, UPPER STERILE lemma awn and sterile hood photo from C. cucullata / C. verticillata / alleged hybrid.
Show true annual crown for C. virgata and separately apex hairs of fertile lemma.
For C. andropogonoides, obtain whole head with ruler and botanical validated spikelet; compare with verticillata.
Source-photo identity for hybrid remains provisional, do not use its photo as a completed taxon confirmation.

handoffs.need: Matched complete mature flowering heads, isolated sterile and fertile lemmas, verified hood/crown of hairs and separate mm-scale awn measurements. No microdiagnostic or microscopic arrow inferred from the present images.

Both species already have canonical species.json and existing licensed photos. Improve specimen-level certainty: slimspike true floral traits and independently vouchered natural hybrid versus parent sterile lemmas; do not re-run first-card admission.
Build from existing photo-rights-filtered assets; verify creator, individual CC licenses, EXIF/GPS stripping, and true Pages deployment. Hybrid remains provisional, not species-FINISHED.

visual_comparison.title: Chloris windmillgrasses — all five installed taxa with real source photos
visual_comparison.subtitle: Eight actual existing photographs inspected October 20. Physical original rights and source metadata retained. Arrows point only to visible radiating racemes, branch junctions and foliage; microscopic hoods, hairs and awns need new macros. Hybrid photo is a SOURCE-ID CANDIDATE.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: WHOLE HEAD → WHERE BRANCHES ATTACH → FERTILE VERSUS UPPER STERILE LEMMA. Some species are inseparable from a distant windmill view.

comparison_cards.title: Hooded versus tumble windmillgrass
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Crowded short versus spaced long branching TIERS; confirm under 10–20×.
comparison_cards.difference: C. cucullata's sterile upper lemma forms a conspicuous rounded HOOD, with short awns. C. verticillata is less hooded with long fertile/sterile lemma awns and spaced whorls.
comparison_cards.caution: Hybrid can be intermediate. Existing heads don't expose a measured hood or awn; no automatic species proof.
photo_roles: head and branch junction same scale

comparison_cards.title: Feather fingergrass versus tumble windmillgrass
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Terminal feathered fan versus spaced whorls + annual versus perennial crown.
comparison_cards.difference: C. virgata typically an annual with long apical fertile-lemma hairs; C. verticillata perennial and often several whorl levels.
comparison_cards.caution: The pictured fuzz cannot be assigned to a particular fertile lemma without dissected spikelets.
photo_roles: true whole head showing whorl spacing

comparison_cards.title: Slimspike versus tumble versus hybrid candidate
comparison_cards.look_here_first: See the entire long thin radiating head; look for whorl tiers and measure two awns in mature spikelets.
comparison_cards.difference: Slimspike may have particularly fine radiating branches, tumble has longer tiered whorls, and source-labeled hybrid can appear intermediate. Awn, fertile/sterile lemma and true hood distinctions are necessary.
comparison_cards.caution: Hybrid photo and slimspike source photo are not independently expert-verified. Intermediate-looking stems alone should not certify hybrid identity.
photo_roles: fertile and sterile lemma profile and awn macro

comparison_cards.title: Hybrid compared with both named parents
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Inspect both parent structures then compare actual upper sterile lemma of putative hybrid.
comparison_cards.difference: C. × subdolichostachya is an accepted hybrid cucullata × verticillata with reported intermediate awn morphology.
comparison_cards.caution: A photograph of a parent is NOT a photo of the hybrid; preserve candidate status until expert morphology confirmed.
photo_roles: two parent photos plainly labeled DIFFERENT TAXA

what_to_teach_crew: For candidate Chloris × subdolichostachya, compare BOTH parent flowering heads at the same scale and isolate the upper STERILE and fertile lemmas; no current photo alone establishes the hybrid.

Hybrid windmillgrass × subdolichostachya IS documented by USDA Welder Germplasm 9085260/PI 645601 (reference only). Its photo candidate is source reported but NOT independently verified. Differentiate fertile lemma 2.2–2.9 mm with 2–5 mm subapical awn from UPPER sterile oblong lemma 1.7–2.2 mm with its own 1–2 mm awn. Confirm actual dissection and both parents; source photo can't prove cross.
